title: The structure of fingernails and toenails
intro: Nails protect the tips of fingers and toes and help with fine movements such as picking up small objects. Each nail is made of hardened keratin, the same protein found in hair, and grows continuously. Changes in nails can reflect local problems and sometimes signs of general illness.

sections.heading: Parts of the nail
paragraphs: The visible nail plate is a hard, translucent plate. It grows from the nail matrix, hidden under the skin at the base, where new cells are formed. The pale half-moon at the base is called the lunula. The nail bed beneath the plate gives it its pink colour. The cuticle seals the gap at the base to prevent germs entering, and the folds on the sides hold the nail in place.

sections.heading: How nails grow
paragraphs: Fingernails grow about three millimetres a month, so a full nail takes roughly four to six months to grow out. Toenails grow more slowly, around one millimetre a month, and take twelve to eighteen months. Growth is faster in summer, in young people and in the dominant hand, and slower with age, poor circulation or illness.

sections.heading: Healthy nails
paragraphs: Healthy nails are smooth and slightly curved, pinkish and firm. Keep them clean and trimmed, avoid biting or picking, protect them from prolonged water and harsh chemicals with gloves, and moisturise hands and cuticles. Do not cut or push back cuticles aggressively. Use nail polish removers sparingly.

sections.heading: Common nail changes
paragraphs: Brittle or splitting nails are often due to repeated wetting or drying. Ridges appear naturally with age, while sudden deep grooves can follow serious illness. White spots usually follow minor injury and are harmless. Pitting or thickening may accompany psoriasis, and yellow, thick nails may signal fungal infection. A dark streak under a nail needs examination to exclude melanoma.

sections.heading: When to see a doctor
paragraphs: See a doctor for painful red swelling around a nail, a nail that detaches without injury, a new dark line, sudden colour changes, clubbing of fingertips or nail changes along with other symptoms such as fatigue or breathlessness.

examples.title: Protecting your nails
examples.text: Imagine your nails split when you wash dishes. You could wear cotton-lined gloves and apply a rich hand cream after washing.

examples.title: Checking a dark line
examples.text: Suppose you notice a new brown streak under a nail. You might arrange a skin and nail check promptly rather than wait.
